description: Decide which ppatlabs tags count as versions at all, and how they order. PROBLEM: a single
ppatlabs build publishes several tag families at once -- 'latest', 'git-<sha>',
'branch-<name>', bare '1', '1.12', '1.12.7', and an immutable '1.12.7-<epoch>' alongside the
mutable '1.12.7'. 'versioning' here is a PARSER CHOICE for that tag soup, NOT an assertion
that ppatlabs follows semver -- read it as a workaround, not as semantics.
The matcher must be the image reference AS WRITTEN in the manifest: the kubernetes manager
sets depName and packageName to the literal string, and all three ppatlabs images here are
written 'docker.io/ppatlabs/<name>'. The previous glob 'ppatlabs/{/,}**' has no leading
wildcard, so it matched none of them: this rule was inert from the day it landed (#559) and
the images silently ran on 'versioning: docker' -- observed in a live 44.30.4 lookup, which
resolved all three to 'versioning: docker' before this fix and to 'semver-coerced' after,
with no change to the updates offered. Both spellings are listed: the registry-prefixed one
used today, and a bare 'ppatlabs/<name>', which is the depName a '# renovate:
datasource=docker depName=...' annotation on the same image would produce. Note the idiom
is '<name>{/,}**' with NO slash before the brace: 'ppatlabs/{/,}**' expands to 'ppatlabs//**'
and 'ppatlabs/**', so the old pattern was wrong twice over.
